This step connects planned DEM collections to provider file metadata for a saved
Stream polygon. An explicit saved-selection download then acquires original
source files with transfer receipts; it does not create analytical terrain/Events.
Study Area discovery remains broader; high-resolution acquisition is Stream-scoped.
Possible mid-resolution Study Area terrain is a separate future workflow.

| Action | Call path | State effect |
|---|---|---|
| Choose Stream/collection | `stream_dem_files_server` reads current Stream sf and explicit DEM plan | Invalidates previous file results |
| Find | `launch_stream_dem_job` → callr → `fluvgeo::discover_stream_dem_files` | Session-only metadata result |
| Resolve | TNM products → exact source-directory match → sf intersection | No guessed collection membership |
| Inspect bounds | child `aoi()` / `files()` → parent shared Leaflet map | Green Stream AOI, purple checked file bounds |
| Save choices | `store$save_dem_files` → `fluvgeo::write_stream_dem_selection` | Immutable file-choice snapshot |
| Reopen | `store$dem_files` → `fluvgeo::read_stream_dem_selection` | Offline read; only current context/source evidence restored |
| Download saved files | `store$prepare_dem_download` → `fluvgeo::prepare_stream_dem_download`; `launch_stream_dem_download_job` → callr → `fluvgeo::run_stream_dem_download` | Exact selection copy, original files and immutable transfer receipts |
| Reopen downloads | `store$dem_download` → background `fluvgeo::read_stream_dem_download` | Offline checksum verification; corrupted/missing assets shown as unavailable |
| Switch/revise/cancel | kill/join worker → `fluvgeo::cancel_stream_dem_download` | Completed receipts retained; only stopped attempt's incomplete files cleaned |

The backend queries OPR or 1 m products only for supported USGS directory links.
It filters metadata bounding boxes, not actual valid-elevation footprints.
COMPLETE is catalog-query completion, not terrain coverage. All catalog pages are
requested before completion; `max_records` is page size, not a total cap. Historic
PARTIAL selections remain readable. FAILED and UNSUPPORTED are not evidence of no available DEMs.
No browser-supplied URL is fetched: endpoints are fixed and collection evidence
comes from the server-held discovery. Unknown resolution/size stays unknown.
Publication date is not survey date. No default scientific suitability follows.

The child `output$acquisition` presents a collapsible download review from the
current checked files, with saved-state comparison. Reported byte sizes are not
measured transfer sizes; missing values produce a known subtotal, not a complete
estimate. Unknown resolution stays unknown and coarser-than-1-m tiles are flagged.
Transfer start is a separate explicit action. Empty results explain that a collection found
for the Study Area may not have any matching tiles for this Stream.

The child module manages a cancellable worker and 45-second per-request timeout,
without a total paging deadline. Changing context revision, discovery, planned candidates,
Stream or collection cancels and clears it, then restores any compatible saved
file choices. Checkboxes remain draft until Save file choices; Select all and Clear
update the same control. Save requires the persisted DEM acquisition plan and
matching source snapshot/raw metadata, Stream geometry and current revision.
Per-pair hashed filenames plus revision tokens prevent stale overwrite; historical
snapshots remain. Switching Stream/collection discards unsaved checkbox drafts.
Refreshing also marks the inventory unsaved even when the returned file IDs are
unchanged. The optimistic file revision token is retained separately, while the
download child receives no saved path until the refreshed evidence is saved.
PARTIAL remains partial even after Select all. The parent owns the one shared map and swaps overlays
when the DEM files tab is active; study geometry and selection snapshots are unchanged.

Sources: `R/stream_dem_files.R`, `R/mod_survey_collections.R`, sibling
`fluvgeo/R/discover_stream_dem_files.R`, `fluvgeo/R/stream_dem_selection.R` and
`R/study_store.R`. Tests: `test-stream-dem-files.R` in Studio,
`test_stream_dem_files.R` in fluvgeo. Opt-in public smoke check:
`dev/scripts/check-stream-dem-files-live.R`. ADR 0007 records the terrain scope and
future multi-source Stream Event/Reach derivative design boundaries.

## Original source downloads (9028)

`stream_dem_download_server` is a child of the DEM file module. The parent supplies
current context, saved path/IDs, draft IDs and a scope reactive. Start requires a
nonempty saved selection matching the checkbox draft. `store$prepare_dem_download`
rechecks the latest context and file-choice revision, saved DEM product intent,
source snapshot/raw metadata and Stream geometry, then prepares a new attempt in
the study's `source-dem` directory. The immutable copied selection is the worker's
input. Later checkbox changes cannot change the active attempt's files.

The separate callr worker runs sequential transfers and writes advisory progress
for the child to poll. Byte counts are measured; percentages appear only with a
usable transfer length. Healthy transfers have no byte or elapsed-time cap.
Connection and idle timeouts identify failed/stalled requests. Failed files have
their own receipts, and later files can still succeed. Explicit start again creates
another attempt, rehashes compatible completed source assets and retries unsuccessful files.

Context/source/saved-selection changes cancel the child job. On cancellation it kills
and joins the process before asking the backend to clean that attempt's numbered
incomplete files. Session end uses the same path. A late result is never attached
to the new scope. Opening a saved attempt launches a verification-only worker;
this reads local files without downloading. Cancellation/error fallback can show
RECORDED, explicitly meaning that a receipt exists but its checksum has not been
rechecked in that view. Full verification distinguishes DOWNLOADED/REUSED from
UNAVAILABLE. A crashed attempt exposes INTERRUPTED/NOT_STARTED work for retry.

Assets use relative content-identifying paths and non-replacing publication.
HTTP/catalog length and TIFF signature checks plus SHA-256 identify transferred
bytes; none establishes raster readability, resolution, vertical datum, coverage
or suitability. The UI remains a compact download action, status and per-file
table. Local destination is expandable. Source and receipt publication
are separate: orphan bytes after a receipt failure do not count as a download.

### Saved availability across refreshed choices (9047/9052)

`store$dem_download_history` locates attempts by Study, Stream and Collection,
independently of the active selection edition. The verification-only callr worker
uses `read_saved_dem_history` to combine outcomes, retaining an available older
copy ahead of a failed retry. Each inspection choice carries its original attempt
path. The **Saved source DEM files** table distinguishes files listed in saved
choices from those saved previously. Availability does not imply inclusion or
scientific acceptance; the existing analysis request binding is unchanged.

Explicit download of refreshed choices can reuse a checksum-verified asset with
the same Collection, file ID and URL and a compatible known byte size. The new
receipt binds the reused bytes to the new snapshot. Remote freshness is not checked.
Historical request byte/duration fields are ignored; connection/idle settings remain.
The next remediation increment will reduce repeated verification reads; this
increment still verifies saved bytes in a background worker.

Additional sources: `R/stream_dem_download.R`, sibling
`fluvgeo/R/stream_dem_download.R` and its `dev/schemas/stream-dem-downloads.md`.
Tests: `test-stream-dem-download.R`, `test-stream-dem-files.R` in Studio and
`test_stream_dem_download.R` in fluvgeo. Transport tests use synthetic bytes and
a loopback HTTP server, never the analyst's saved tile choices.
